intro: Professionals and everyday users convert grams (g) to troy ounces (oz t) when working across metric and other standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One gram equals 0.032151 troy ounces, while 1 troy ounce equals 31.103477 grams. Whether you are verifying mass & weight specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Avoirdupois Ounces (oz) vs. Precious Metal Troy Ounces (oz t) vs. Fluid Ounces (fl oz)
items: Standard grocery and postal scales use the Avoirdupois ounce (1 oz = 28.349523125 g). Gold, silver, and platinum bullion use the Troy ounce (1 oz t = 31.1034768 g), which is 9.7% heavier.
Never confuse dry weight ounces (oz) with liquid volume fluid ounces (fl oz); they only match numerically for pure water at standard density.

faqs.question: How many troy ounces (oz t) are in 1 gram (g)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.03215075 troy ounces (oz t) in 1 gram (g), which rounds to 0.0322 oz t for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 troy ounce equals 31.103477 grams.

faqs.question: How do I convert grams to troy ounces (g to oz t)?
faqs.answer: To convert grams to troy ounces, use the formula: oz t = g × 0.03215075. For example, converting 100 g gives 3.2151 oz t.

faqs.question: What is 100 grams in troy ounces?
faqs.answer: 100 grams (g) equals exactly 3.2151 troy ounces (oz t) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
